messages:
maya: Hi team — enterprise customer reported their April invoice is ~17% higher than what the dashboard and our SDK estimator predict. They run a heavy chat+tool workflow. SDK local estimator for the session: prompt=512, completion=533, total=1045. Invoice shows total=1223. I can repro locally. trace_id=tr-abc123

sam: Thanks, can you paste a minimal repro (curl + estimator output)? Also include any server metering log you grabbed.

maya: Pasting a sanitized repro below. Note: this is single conversation thread, no streaming, one tool call in the middle.

maya: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that formats answers as bullets."},{"role":"user","content":"Give me a TL;DR of the below article."},{"role":"tool","name":"web_search","content":"search results..."}], "stream": false}'
```

maya: SDK estimator output (python sdk v0.8.2):
maya: ```
Estimator: prompt_tokens=512, completion_tokens=533, total_tokens=1045
```

maya: Server metering log (from internal meter trace for tr-abc123):
maya: ```
metering: prompt_tokens=628, completion_tokens=595, total_tokens=1223, note=server_injected_system_prefix, trace_id=tr-abc123
```

jordan: Interesting — server shows +116 prompt tokens vs estimator. That smells like an injected system prefix or tool-call framing on the server side that our local estimator doesn't account for. Any chance the private deployment or routing applied a preamble?

maya: Customer is on Hosted API (not private). We suspect one of these: 1) runtime inserts an internal system prompt for telemetry/error-context; 2) tool responses are wrapped with metadata (e.g., function_name, metadata blocks) that are counted server-side but not by estimator; 3) streaming/resume boundaries added extra EOS tokens in billing.

sam: Can you attach the full metering debug block? If unavailable, please repro with header X-Redwood-Meter-Debug: 1 to get per-component token breakdown (server preamble, tool-wrapping, kv-metadata). That header will return a meter_breakdown in the response body.

maya: I retried with the debug header. Response includes:
maya: ```json
{ "meter_breakdown": { "client_prompt": 512, "server_preamble": 116, "tool_wrapping": 0, "client_completion": 595 } }
```

lee: That matches the delta. If meter_breakdown.server_preamble exists we need to decide whether SDK estimator should surface it or not. For hosted customers the preamble is internal and not returned to clients, but it is billable.

jordan: For immediate support: 1) Notify billing with trace_id so they can map invoice lines. 2) For transparency, update SDK estimator to optionally include server-side preamble guess (config flag estimate_server_prefix=true) so customers can approximate invoice. 3) Long-term: product decision — either make server preamble non-billable for PLG/free tiers or document it clearly.

maya: Confirmed billing has the trace_id and is reviewing. Customer asks for repro script to validate locally. Here's a minimal repro suggestion: use the same model + messages and include header to request meter debug: 
maya: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Meter-Debug: 1' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize this long doc..."}], "stream": false }'
```

sam: Good. For SDK teams: open a small bug/feature to add an "estimated_server_prefix_tokens" field to the estimator output. Use a conservative default (100-150 tokens) and make it opt-in so it doesn't surprise existing users.

lee: Also double-check function/tool metadata handling. We saw some tool integrations that add a JSON envelope with keys and provenance in the server side which can add tokens. If the estimator only counts raw content it will undercount.

billing-bot: Invoice entry matched: invoice_2026_04 line-item total 1223 tokens for customer XYZ, trace_id=tr-abc123. Billing team will send a detailed breakdown to the account owner once support confirms repro.

maya: Action items: 1) I will escalate to billing and attach the meter debug and trace. 2) Sam — please file SDK estimator opt-in flag (estimate_server_prefix). 3) Eng (jordan/lee) — can you confirm whether hosted runtime will always inject server_preamble for this workflow? If so, we should add a KB note.

sam: Filed: SDK-4567 "opt-in estimate_server_prefix_tokens (nullable int)". Assigned to devex.

jordan: I'll check runtime routing rules and come back with whether the preamble is deterministic or applied for specific toolchains (e.g., web_search).

maya: Thanks. Customer notified we will follow up with a breakdown and (if needed) a bill adjustment. :eyes:

lee: FYI — if others run into this, quick triage checklist: 1) request meter debug header, 2) check meter_breakdown.server_preamble, 3) see if tool_wrapping or kv_metadata contributed, 4) attach trace_id to billing ticket.

maya: Will do. Closing loop here once billing confirms.
